stem: A marketing director asks why the company should train staff in prompt engineering when the same Gemini model is available to everyone. Which statement best describes the value of prompt engineering?

choices.text: It retrains the model on the company's private documents so that the model permanently stores the brand's facts in its weights
It crafts and iteratively refines the instructions, context and examples sent to the model, so the same model gives more relevant output
It replaces the foundation model with a smaller one that is selected automatically for each request based on the prompt length
It guarantees that the model will never produce an incorrect statement, so staff no longer need to review the generated drafts

stem: A communications team wants a model to turn a long press release into a three-sentence summary and to translate a short customer notice into Spanish. Both are common tasks with no company-specific format. Which prompting approach is the simplest suitable choice?

choices.text: Few-shot prompting with at least ten carefully written summary and translation pairs for each of the two tasks, reviewed by editors first
Prompt chaining with a separate prompt for reading, outlining, drafting, and polishing each of the two tasks
Zero-shot prompting, giving a clear instruction and the text with no examples, since both tasks are well known to the model
ReAct prompting that lets the model call a search tool before it writes the summary or the translation

stem: A support team needs a model to label each incoming email as Billing, Outage, Feature Request or Account Access, and to return only the label in a fixed format used by the ticketing system. A plain instruction produces labels in varying wording. What should the team add to the prompt?

choices.text: Several example emails each paired with the exact label text the ticketing system expects, plus the instruction itself
A role statement saying the model is a senior support manager with twenty years of experience in customer service
A follow-up prompt that asks the model to rewrite its answer in a friendlier tone before it is stored in the system
An instruction to think step by step and describe in detail why each email fits its category before the label

stem: A product team has a single approved sample of how its release-note headlines should read. They want the model to write new headlines in the same style. Which description of the prompt is accurate?

choices.text: Prompt chaining, because the sample headline is passed from one prompt to the next as the working output
Few-shot prompting, because any prompt that includes an example is few-shot, however many it holds
Zero-shot prompting, because the sample is only a style guide and is not counted as an example by the model
One-shot prompting, because the prompt holds a single example that shows the model the target style

stem: A bank wants its internal assistant to explain mortgage terms to first-time buyers in a patient, plain-language way, avoiding jargon and never giving personal financial advice. Which technique most directly sets this behavior for every answer?

choices.text: Zero-shot prompting with no persona or limits, relying on the model's general knowledge of mortgage terms
ReAct prompting, letting the assistant call a mortgage-rate tool before it explains each term to the buyer
Role prompting: system instructions giving a friendly mortgage-advisor persona plus its constraints
Chain-of-thought prompting, asking the model to list every calculation step it uses before it replies to the buyer

stem: A consulting firm wants an assistant to read a 40-page customer feedback document, extract the main complaints, group them into themes, and then draft an executive email with recommendations. A single large prompt gives shallow, inconsistent results. What is the best technique?

choices.text: Prompt chaining: run a prompt to extract complaints, a second to group them into themes, and a third to draft the email
Role prompting only, telling the model it is a world-class consultant who always writes excellent executive emails
Zero-shot prompting repeated several times with the same long instruction until one response looks acceptable
Increase the number of examples in a single prompt until the model returns the finished email in one response

stem: A finance team asks a model to work out the total cost of a project with three stages, each with a different discount rule. The model often states a wrong total with no explanation. Which prompting change is most likely to improve accuracy?

choices.text: Provide a single unrelated example about writing a poem so the model learns to follow instructions
Ask the model to work through the problem step by step, showing its reasoning, before it gives the total
Ask the model for the shortest possible answer so that it spends no effort on irrelevant text
Give the model a persona of a certified accountant and tell it to answer with complete confidence

stem: An online retailer wants a customer assistant that can answer "Where is my order and can it still be changed?" The answer depends on live order data held in an internal system, which the model cannot know from training. Which technique fits best?

choices.text: Chain-of-thought prompting alone, asking the model to reason step by step about what an order status could be
Zero-shot prompting with a polite persona, so the model answers courteously whatever it knows about the order
Few-shot prompting with sample orders, so that the model memorizes the status of every customer's current shipment
ReAct prompting, where the model alternates reasoning about what it needs with actions such as calling the order system

stem: A team lead is deciding between chain-of-thought and ReAct prompting for two projects: a tool that checks the logic of a long contract clause using only the text pasted in, and a travel assistant that must check live flight availability while planning. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: ReAct for both, because ReAct is required whenever a task has more than one step to carry out
Chain-of-thought for the contract clause, because the text is self-contained, and ReAct for the travel assistant
Chain-of-thought for both, because reasoning steps alone are enough to retrieve live flight availability
ReAct for the contract clause, because long texts always need tools, and chain-of-thought for the travel assistant

stem: A team added four examples to its prompt for classifying survey comments but wrote no instructions beyond "Here are some examples." Nearly all four examples were positive comments, and the model now labels almost every new comment as positive. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The examples were too few for the foundation model to function at all, so the model returned the same label by default
Zero-shot prompting always overrides examples, so the model ignored the four samples and answered at random
Without clear instructions and with unbalanced examples, the model learned an unintended pattern from the samples
The model has run out of its knowledge cutoff window, so it can no longer analyze the sentiment of recent comments

stem: A retailer wants product descriptions in a specific brand voice. It has about a dozen approved descriptions and needs a working pilot this week, with no machine learning staff available. What is the best first approach?

choices.text: Use few-shot prompting with several approved descriptions and a brand-voice instruction, and test before considering heavier customization
Build a new model from scratch using the descriptions as the full training set, since they define the voice
Fine-tune a foundation model on the approved descriptions and release it to pilot users only after the tuned model is evaluated
Wait until the company has thousands of labeled descriptions, because prompts cannot influence voice at all

stem: An HR team wants the model to draft policy summaries that staff will actually follow. Which TWO additions to a basic prompt are consistent with Google's prompt design guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Removal of all instructions so the model can decide for itself which format the summary takes
A rule that the prompt should never contain context, because extra background always confuses the model
Repetition of the same instruction six times in slightly different words to emphasize it
A statement of the audience, tone and required format, such as plain-language bullets for new employees
One or two short sample summaries that show the expected structure and level of detail

stem: A claims department wants an assistant that handles a complex claim in sequence: read the claim, check each fact against the policy database, decide whether more information is needed, and then draft a decision letter. Which TWO techniques would work together best? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Removing any intermediate output, because showing the steps is unhelpful for tasks that need review
Zero-shot prompting alone, since the policy database is unnecessary when the model has seen insurance documents
A short persona sentence as the only technique, because tone alone determines whether the decision is correct
ReAct prompting, so the assistant can look up policy records through tools while it reasons about the claim
Prompt chaining, so that reading, checking and letter drafting run as connected steps whose outputs feed each other

stem: A team asks a model to solve multi-step scheduling puzzles. Their examples show the final answer first and then a step-by-step explanation written afterward. The model gives confident but wrong answers. Which change is most likely to help?

choices.text: Replace the examples with a request for the final answer in as few words as possible
Reorder the examples so that the reasoning steps come first and the final answer follows from them
Move the examples to a separate earlier prompt so that they are not visible to the model while it works on the puzzle
Add a persona stating that the model is an expert and must never be wrong

stem: A retail bank wants its developers to try several models for a document-summarization project: a Google model, a partner model and an open-weights model. The bank wants to compare them side by side and deploy the winner without building separate integrations for each provider. Which Google Cloud capability fits this need?

choices.text: Model Garden in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, a central catalog where developers discover, test and deploy first-party, partner and open models
Gemini for Google Workspace, which lets each employee choose a preferred model provider inside Docs and Gmail
Agent Search, which gives developers a ready-made search application over the bank's documents and compares model providers automatically
Agent Platform AutoML, which trains and compares candidate models of different providers from the bank's labeled documents

stem: A media company's developers want to run an open-weights model but have no team to provision or operate servers. They want to call it through a managed API. Which approach on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits best?

choices.text: Export the open model to the company's own data center and expose it through an API gateway that the developers operate
Ask Agent Search to import the open model's weights, then publish it as a search widget on the company website
Pick the open model in Model Garden and use it as a Model as a Service offering, which Google serves through a managed API
Train a new open-weights model from scratch with Agent Platform AutoML, so that Google can host the finished model for the company

stem: A subscription retailer has a table of customer history, such as purchases, support tickets and plan type, with a column showing who cancelled. The marketing team wants a model that predicts which customers are likely to cancel. The company has no data scientists and no machine learning engineers. Which option on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which trains a prediction model from the labeled table without requiring data science expertise or code
Agent Search, by indexing the customer table so that marketers can search for customers who look like churners
Model Garden, by deploying a large open language model and asking it to guess churn from each customer's raw row of data
Custom training, where an engineer writes a training application and chooses the algorithm and hyperparameters

stem: A research group wants a model for an unusual scientific objective that is not one of the standard prediction tasks. The group needs its own loss function and full control over the training environment. A colleague proposes Agent Platform AutoML because it is the fastest to set up. What is the best response?

choices.text: Use Agent Search, because it can learn an arbitrary objective from the group's clickstream events
Use Gemini for Google Workspace, because it can train custom scientific models from documents in a shared drive
Use custom training instead, because AutoML only supports predefined objectives and limits control of the training process
Keep AutoML, because it can accept any objective and custom loss function if the group raises its training budget

stem: A software vendor wants customers to find answers on its public documentation website using natural-language questions. The vendor's small web team has little machine learning experience and wants results that include generated summaries with links back to the pages. Which Google Cloud offering is the best fit?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which trains a text classification model from labeled examples that sorts each documentation page into a fixed set of topics for editors
Agent Search, which provides semantic search, generative answers and summaries over the vendor's content, with a widget for the site
Model Garden alone, because choosing a model there automatically indexes the website and adds a search box to it
Custom training of a new language model from scratch on the documentation, hosted by the web team on virtual machines

stem: A streaming service wants viewers to find movies and music through natural-language queries, and wants each viewer to see recommendations tailored to what they watch. The service wants managed capabilities rather than building ranking models itself. Which offering should it evaluate first?

choices.text: A Gemini Enterprise notebook that each editor fills with a playlist for every individual viewer
Contact center agents built with Conversational Agents, which answer phone calls from viewers about their subscriptions
Agent Platform AutoML tabular models only, trained once and queried through a spreadsheet by the editorial team
Agent Search, which includes media search and media recommendations that are tuned for content such as movies, videos and music

stem: An executive asks what RAG Engine in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform does for the company. Which description is most accurate?

choices.text: It permanently retrains the foundation model on the company's documents, so the private knowledge is stored in the model's weights
It filters all prompts for harmful content before they reach the model, and it does not use any company data
It replaces the company's databases with a vector store, which becomes the single system of record for all business data
It connects a model to private data, retrieving relevant passages at question time for better context

stem: A developer team is building a custom assistant on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform that must answer from the company's internal files. Select TWO steps that RAG Engine manages in this process. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replacing the user's question with a fixed answer from a lookup table
Approving each generated answer before it is shown to the user
Ingesting data from sources such as Cloud Storage or Google Drive
Retraining the foundation model's weights on every new document
Indexing the transformed data into a searchable corpus

stem: A company has two projects. The first needs a working question-answering experience over its intranet pages within weeks, with minimal developer effort. The second is a custom application whose developers want to control how data is chunked, which corpus is searched and how retrieved context feeds their own agent logic. Which pairing of Google Cloud RAG offerings matches?

choices.text: Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for the first project, and RAG Engine for the second
Prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for both, because only that offering can use company data
Model Garden for the first project, and Agent Platform AutoML for the second
RAG Engine for the first project, and prebuilt RAG with Agent Search for the second

stem: A legal team's assistant, built on a general foundation model, confidently quotes outdated clause wording from its training. The firm's current templates are stored in Cloud Storage and change monthly. The firm does not want to retrain a model every month. Which change addresses the problem?

choices.text: Move the templates to Model Garden, where the platform automatically teaches every hosted model the newest wording from those files
Add RAG: index the templates with RAG Engine so that current clauses are retrieved and supplied to the model with each question
Retrain the foundation model from scratch each month on the new templates so the weights always match them
Lower the response length limit so the assistant has less room to include outdated wording

stem: A software architect describes Agent Development Kit (ADK) to the business sponsor of a new customer-service agent project. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: ADK is an open-source, model-agnostic framework that developers use to build and deploy agents, from simple tasks to complex workflows
ADK is a no-code chat window where business users type instructions and an agent is produced without any developer involvement
ADK is a pre-trained foundation model that Google hosts exclusively for use with the Gemini family
ADK is a billing tool that tracks the usage and cost of each agent after it has been deployed

stem: A developer team has built a custom agent and now needs to run it in production. The company wants Google to handle the infrastructure, scaling and built-in observability so the team can focus on the application. Which part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform fits?

choices.text: Agent Platform AutoML, which hosts any agent code after it trains a prediction model of the agent's behavior on past conversations
A Compute Engine virtual machine group that the team patches, sizes and scales itself
Agent Runtime, a fully managed environment to deploy, operate and scale agents without managing the underlying infrastructure
Agent Search, which converts agent code into a website search widget for the production environment

stem: A company's engineers already use an open-source agent framework they know well and do not want to rewrite their agents. Leadership still wants Google Cloud's managed models, search and grounding services. How does Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform support this?

choices.text: The company must choose between its framework and Google Cloud's grounding services, because the two cannot be used together
Developers may use ADK or any other open-source framework, call Gemini or any model in Model Garden, and use platform services such as RAG
Agent Platform supports only Google-built models, so the company must drop its framework and its other model providers
Only agents written with ADK can access models and services, so the engineers must rewrite their agents before using Agent Platform

stem: An insurance company's CIO is explaining the business value of building agents on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform instead of assembling separate tools. Select TWO statements that are accurate. (Select TWO)

choices.text: The platform requires all company data to be copied into Google's public model training sets before any agent can use it
Using the platform guarantees that an agent will never produce an incorrect answer
Agents built on the platform can use only a single model family chosen at project creation
Agents can be grounded on the enterprise's own data through services such as RAG Engine and Agent Search
One platform covers the full lifecycle: building agents, deploying and scaling them, and governing them

stem: A product team needs two things. First, a model that classifies photographs of building types into categories using the team's own labeled images, with no coding. Second, a way for support staff to ask questions about the team's product manuals and get cited answers. Select TWO products that match these needs, one for each need. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Agent Runtime, for classifying the photographs without any model
Model Garden, for training the image classifier with the team's labeled photographs
RAG Engine, for training the image classifier by chunking the photographs
Agent Search, for natural-language answers over the product manuals
Agent Platform AutoML, for the image classification model trained on the labeled photographs

stem: A manufacturer's leadership team is deciding between Agent Search, RAG Engine and Model Garden for three initiatives. Initiative X is a customer-facing help search with generated answers and an embeddable widget. Initiative Y is a custom agent whose developers want to design retrieval themselves. Initiative Z is a team evaluating which available models write the best product descriptions. Which mapping is correct?

choices.text: X uses Model Garden, Y uses Agent Search, and Z uses RAG Engine
X uses Agent Search, Y uses RAG Engine, and Z uses Model Garden
X, Y and Z all use Model Garden, since every Agent Platform service is accessed through it
X uses RAG Engine, Y uses Model Garden, and Z uses Agent Search

stem: A retailer's AI team wants to test a Google model, an open-source model and a partner model on the same product-description task before committing to one. The CIO wants this comparison done on a single managed platform rather than by stitching together three vendors' tooling. Which strength of Google Cloud's approach addresses this need?

choices.text: An open approach in which Model Garden offers Google, open-source and partner models side by side to discover, test, customize and deploy
An infrastructure-only approach in which Google supplies the servers and the retailer hosts each model with its own tooling
A pre-built application approach in which a finished Google app is configured by users and no model comparison is possible
A closed approach in which every workload must use a single Google-built model, so that results are consistent across all teams

stem: A bank has built agents on a platform that lets it change the underlying model whenever a better or cheaper one appears. The risk team asks what the bank gives up each time the model is changed. Which statement reflects the benefit Google describes for its open, multi-model platform?

choices.text: The bank must rebuild its tool connections and identity policies each time, but gains a better model with every change
The bank can swap only between Google-built models, because partner and open-source models use incompatible controls
The bank can swap models while keeping its underlying logic, tool connections and identity policies intact
The bank can swap models only at the end of a contract term, when Google re-provisions the agents on the new model

stem: A healthcare company wants to use Google's gen AI services with its own confidential documents. Its legal team asks first whether Google will use the company's data to train or fine-tune models without being asked. Which statement describes Google Cloud's enterprise-ready position?

choices.text: Google will use the data only to train models that the company later receives, and never for any other customer's models
Google may use the prompts for training by default and the company must file a request each month to opt out of it
Google does not use customer data to train or fine-tune AI/ML models without the customer's prior permission or instruction
Google lets the company choose training use only after it upgrades from the standard service to a premium support tier

stem: A financial regulator requires a bank to control the encryption keys that protect the data it stores for its gen AI projects, including their location, rotation schedule and who may use them. By default, Google encrypts the content at rest. Which capability meets the requirement?

choices.text: A larger model choice, because bigger models apply stronger encryption to the data they process
A prompt-engineering policy that tells employees not to include sensitive details in the text sent to a model
Google default encryption, which already gives the bank direct control of rotation schedules and key access permissions
CMEK in Cloud KMS, giving the bank control over key protection level, location, rotation and access

stem: A research lab will train a very large model whose computation consists mostly of large matrix operations. The lab asks what Google-designed hardware exists for this. Which hardware, and which benefit, should the cloud adviser describe?

choices.text: General-purpose CPUs only, because matrix-heavy models are best trained on processors built for flexibility with many small tasks
Cloud TPUs, custom chips for large matrix operations with high-bandwidth memory, connectable in slices
Local hard disks on each server, because training speed depends mainly on where the training files are stored
Edge devices at customer sites, because distributing the training across users' phones is how Google scales large models

stem: A media company already has gen AI code written around a popular GPU-oriented framework with many custom operations. Its leaders want to know whether Google Cloud forces a move to Google's own chips. Which description of Google Cloud's AI infrastructure is accurate?

choices.text: Both NVIDIA GPUs and Google Cloud TPUs are offered, so the company can choose the accelerator that fits each workload
Accelerators are offered only on premises, so the company must buy hardware before running its workloads
Only NVIDIA GPUs are offered, because Google's custom chips are reserved for Google's internal products
Only Google's TPUs are offered, so the company must rewrite its code for them before it can use any accelerator

stem: A company plans to train and serve large gen AI models and does not want to assemble accelerators, networking, storage and orchestration software from separate sources. Which Google Cloud offering is described as an integrated supercomputing system optimized for AI and ML workloads?

choices.text: Looker, a business intelligence platform that visualizes data but does not train or serve models
AI Hypercomputer, combining optimized infrastructure, open software and flexible consumption options
Cloud Storage, an object store that holds training data but does not provide accelerators or orchestration
Cloud Run, a serverless service that runs stateless containers and scales them to zero when idle

stem: An operations executive asks which TWO benefits Google associates with AI Hypercomputer for a company that trains and serves gen AI models. (Select TWO)

choices.text: It guarantees that every model it runs is free of bias without any evaluation by the company
It restricts the company to a single framework, which simplifies the choice of software
It maximizes goodput, so accelerators spend more time on productive computation and less on system overhead
It removes the need for any data to be stored, because models learn directly from their prompts
It provides high-throughput storage options that help remove I/O bottlenecks during training

stem: A manufacturer wants employees to ask one question and get answers from content spread across Google Workspace, Microsoft SharePoint, Jira and other business apps. Executives insist that people see only what they are already allowed to see. Which strength of Google's AI ecosystem fits?

choices.text: A data export that copies all files into one shared folder that every employee can open
A public web search that indexes every internal file and shows the same results to all employees regardless of access rights
A separate chatbot per app, so employees must ask each tool individually and combine the results themselves
One Gemini-powered search and assistant with prebuilt connectors to business apps, giving permissions-aware answers

stem: A global company has dozens of teams building agents. The CIO fears "agent sprawl" and wants IT to see, index, manage and reuse agents from one place and enforce consistent policies. Which Google Cloud capability addresses this governance need?

choices.text: A single control plane using Agent Registry and Agent Gateway for central discovery, reuse and policy enforcement
A requirement that all agents be built by one central team so that no other team can build agents
A per-team spreadsheet in which each team lists its agents and applies the policies it prefers
A larger foundation model, because a more capable model automatically enforces company policy on every agent

stem: An auditor reviewing a company's agents asks how the company can trace and audit what each agent did, and limit what each one can access. Which TWO capabilities from Google Cloud's agent platform help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Audit logging is turned off for agents so that sensitive prompts are never written anywhere
All agents share one administrator account, so every action is recorded under the same name
Agents inherit the access of whichever employee created them, with no separate permissions
Each agent receives its own cryptographically secure identity, so its actions can be attributed to it
Least-privilege IAM controls limit what each agent is allowed to access

stem: A marketing team with no programmers wants to build a simple automated process that runs in the background, while the company's engineers want to build more advanced agents in code. Which pair of Google offerings reflects Google's effort to make AI available to both groups?

choices.text: A no-access policy for business users, and a code-only toolkit that is kept for a central research team
A low-code option with templates for business users, and the Agent Development Kit for professional developers
A spreadsheet macro for business users, and a hardware order form for professional developers
A single code-only toolkit for both groups, with business users expected to learn programming first

stem: A small insurer has no data scientists and no budget to train models from scratch, but it wants to add text summarization and image generation to a claims app quickly. Which Google Cloud approach reflects "democratizing AI" for this insurer?

choices.text: Call pre-trained Google models through APIs, customizing them later only if the results need improvement
Wait until a ready-made claims application exists, because gen AI cannot be added to existing apps
Purchase a dedicated accelerator cluster first, then decide which features the app should offer
Collect a large claims dataset and train a custom foundation model before adding any feature to the app

stem: A company worries that its agents will need custom connectors to reach each internal database and business system. Which part of Google Cloud's open approach reduces this effort?

choices.text: A proprietary connector format that works only with systems purchased from Google
A manual process in which an engineer copies data into each agent's prompt every morning
Native support for open standards such as MCP and OpenAPI, so agents connect to existing systems
A requirement to migrate every internal database into a Google-built data store before any agent can use it

stem: A global brand wants to create localized campaigns containing images, audio and video, and the security team insists that all generation happen on one governed enterprise platform instead of several unrelated consumer tools. Which strength of Google Cloud supports this?

choices.text: Google's generative media models, such as Veo, available alongside text models on one secure enterprise platform
A restriction to text generation only, so images, audio and video must be produced outside the platform
A requirement that each campaign team subscribe to a different external tool and upload brand assets to it
A public website where staff paste confidential brand assets so that anyone can view the generated results

stem: A bank's executive team keeps hearing "AI", "machine learning" and "generative AI" used as if they were the same thing. A leader wants to explain how they relate. Which description is accurate?

choices.text: Generative AI is the broad field of all intelligent software; ML is one of its products, and AI is the name for the content these models produce
Machine learning is the broad field of intelligent systems; artificial intelligence is a subset of it that uses data, and generative AI is the older rule-based approach it replaced
Artificial intelligence and generative AI are the same thing under two names, while machine learning refers only to storing historical data in a warehouse for reporting
AI is the broad field of machines doing tasks that need human intelligence; machine learning is a subset that learns from data; gen AI is a subset of ML that creates content

stem: A retailer uses a model that reads an email and decides whether it is spam, and now wants a second system that writes a first draft of a reply to a customer complaint. Which statement correctly separates the two systems?

choices.text: Both are generative AI, because any model that processes email text is generating content about it
The spam filter is a predictive (discriminative) model that assigns a label; the reply drafter is generative AI that produces new text
Neither is machine learning, because both operate on text and machine learning only applies to numeric tables
The spam filter is generative AI because it creates a spam label, and the reply drafter is a classifier because it picks from a fixed list of replies

stem: A call-center director asks what natural language processing (NLP) contributes to a virtual agent that understands what customers type and answers in sentences. Which description of NLP is correct?

choices.text: NLP is a reinforcement-learning method in which a model earns rewards for repeating a fixed script word for word
NLP is a data-governance practice that removes personal information from conversations before they are stored
NLP is the AI field that lets computers interpret, understand and generate human language, as in chatbots and translation
NLP is a hardware design that speeds up the matrix operations behind model training in large data centers

stem: A media company's CIO asks what makes a "foundation model" different from the narrow models the analytics team trained in the past, each built for one task. Which answer is correct?

choices.text: A foundation model is a database layer that stores the company's documents so other models can read them
A foundation model is trained on a very large, broad dataset so that one model can be adapted to many tasks instead of training one per task
A foundation model is a small model that only works after it is trained from scratch on the company's private tables for one prediction task
A foundation model is any model with a rule-based decision tree written by experts for a single regulated process

stem: An insurance company wants one system that accepts a photo of a damaged car and a typed description, then produces a written summary of the likely damage. Which type of model fits this need?

choices.text: A reinforcement-learning agent trained from scratch by rewarding it for correct repair estimates
A text-only LLM, because the description is the only input that matters
An image-only classification model, because the photo is the only input that matters
A multimodal foundation model that can take images and text together as input and produce text

stem: A design agency wants a model that turns a short text description into a brand-new illustration. A consultant explains that many leading image generators are "diffusion models". Which statement describes diffusion models correctly?

choices.text: They compress existing images into smaller files so large design assets cost less to store
They sort a customer's existing images into groups of similar pictures without using any labels at all
They start from random noise and refine it step by step into an image that fits the description
They search a library of existing illustrations and return the stored image that most closely matches the description

stem: A legal-services firm wants a system that reads long contracts, answers questions about them in natural language and drafts clause summaries. Which kind of model is the core of such a system?

choices.text: A large language model, trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language
A time-series forecasting model, which predicts a future numeric value from past values
A clustering algorithm, which groups similar contracts without producing text
A diffusion model, trained to turn random noise into images

stem: A product manager is told that an LLM usage report is measured in "tokens" and asks a colleague what a token is. Which answer is accurate?

choices.text: A token is a security credential that proves a user is allowed to call the model
A token is a complete sentence, so a 500-word document always counts as exactly the same number of tokens
A token is a labeled example in the training set that tells the model the correct answer for one input
A token is a unit of text, such as a word, part of a word or punctuation mark, that the model reads and generates

stem: A company has years of past loan applications, each marked "repaid" or "defaulted". It wants a model to predict the outcome for new applicants. Which machine learning approach applies, and why?

choices.text: Unsupervised learning, because the model must discover which applicants are likely to default without ever being told any outcomes
Supervised learning, because every historical record includes its correct outcome, which the model learns to predict
Reinforcement learning, because the model should earn rewards for approving loans
Generative AI, because any prediction about a person requires a model that writes new text

stem: A marketing team has data on millions of customers' purchases but no predefined segments. It wants an algorithm to discover natural groups of similar shoppers so campaigns can be tailored. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Unsupervised learning, such as clustering, which finds groups in unlabeled data
A prompt-engineering exercise, since segments can only be created by writing instructions to an LLM
Reinforcement learning, where an agent is penalized each time a customer ignores an email
Supervised classification, trained on shopper groups that the team defines by hand for every customer

stem: A logistics firm wants software that learns how to route warehouse robots by trying actions in a simulated warehouse and receiving a reward for fast, collision-free deliveries. Which ML approach does this describe?

choices.text: Supervised learning, because every robot movement was labeled in advance with the right answer by human experts
Diffusion modeling, because the robots start from noise and refine their route
Reinforcement learning, because an agent learns a strategy by interacting with an environment and maximizing rewards
Unsupervised learning, because the robots group packages by similarity

stem: A hospital group is listing which of its projects use which ML approach. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Teaching a scheduling agent to improve operating-room use through rewards for shorter waits: reinforcement learning
Grouping patients with similar symptom histories when no categories are defined in advance: supervised learning
Predicting length of stay from labeled records: unsupervised learning
Discovering unusual billing patterns from unlabeled claims where nobody defined the outcome: reinforcement learning
Predicting readmission using past patients' records that include a known readmitted/not-readmitted outcome: supervised learning

stem: A communications team tells colleagues it is doing "prompt engineering" with an existing LLM. Which description of that work is accurate?

choices.text: They are retraining the entire model on a new dataset so that its internal weights change permanently across the company
They are refining the instructions, context and examples in the input, without changing the model itself, to get better outputs
They are building a new data warehouse so the model can retrieve numeric data faster
They are deploying the model to additional regions so responses arrive faster

stem: A team is told it can adapt an LLM in two ways, prompt engineering or prompt tuning. A leader wants the high-level difference. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Both terms mean writing better wording, and the only difference is that prompt tuning is done by developers
Prompt engineering trains extra parameters on a labeled dataset, while prompt tuning is a person rewriting the prompt wording
Prompt engineering changes the model's architecture, while prompt tuning only changes the font of the output
Prompt engineering adjusts prompt text by hand, while prompt tuning trains a few added parameters with the base model frozen

stem: A support team has an LLM that gives acceptable but inconsistent answers. The team has no labeled examples, no ML staff and a deadline next week. What should leaders recommend first?

choices.text: Switch to reinforcement learning so the model rewards itself for consistent wording
Wait to collect and label a large dataset of examples, then run a tuning job before any pilot starts
Start with prompt engineering: add clear instructions, a role, a format and a few examples, then iterate
Train a brand-new foundation model from scratch so the answers are fully under the company's control

stem: An executive wants a one-slide picture of the machine learning lifecycle. Which sequence of stages is correct?

choices.text: Data preparation, data ingestion, model management, model training, model deployment
Data ingestion, data preparation, model training, model deployment, model management
Model training, data ingestion, data preparation, model deployment, model management
Data ingestion, model deployment, data preparation, model training, model management

stem: A ride-sharing company receives a continuous stream of trip events from millions of phones and wants to collect them reliably as the first stage of its ML lifecycle. Which Google Cloud service is designed to ingest streaming event data?

choices.text: Pub/Sub, a messaging service that ingests and distributes streaming events at scale
Model Registry, a repository for versions of trained models
Looker, a tool that only visualizes results after the data is already organized
Cloud Storage Archive class, a storage class meant for data accessed less than once a year

stem: A manufacturer's raw sensor data has arrived in Google Cloud, but it contains duplicates, missing readings and different units. The data team must clean and transform it at scale before any training. Which lifecycle stage is this, and which tool fits?

choices.text: Model management, using monitoring to detect drift in the sensor values
Data ingestion, using Pub/Sub to correct duplicates and unit differences
Model deployment, using a prediction endpoint to serve the sensor readings back to the factory systems
Data preparation, using a data-processing service such as Dataflow, or BigQuery for SQL-based transformations

stem: A retailer has prepared its tabular sales data and wants a business-analytics team with limited ML expertise to build a good prediction model quickly, with Google Cloud managing the training infrastructure. Which approach suits the model training stage?

choices.text: Use Pub/Sub to train the model, since it reliably handles large streams of data coming from many different sources
Skip training and deploy a blank model to an endpoint so it learns on its own
Use AutoML on Agent Platform, which trains models from managed datasets without hand-written algorithms or servers
Build a custom hardware cluster in a private data center and install and tune the training software by hand

stem: A data science team needs an interactive environment where its members can explore data, write and test code, and develop custom models before running larger training jobs. Which Google Cloud tool serves this need in the ML lifecycle?

choices.text: Pub/Sub, which queues messages between applications
Cloud Armor, which filters malicious web traffic before it reaches an application
Workbench on Agent Platform, a managed notebook environment for exploring data and developing models
Model Registry, which only stores finished model versions and does not offer a coding environment

stem: A bank has a trained model and now wants its mobile app to obtain predictions from it in real time, without the bank running prediction servers. Which lifecycle stage is this, and which capability fits?

choices.text: Model deployment, by deploying the model to an Agent Platform endpoint that serves online predictions
Model management, by exporting the model into a spreadsheet that staff then query manually each time
Model training, by retraining the model every time the app asks for a prediction
Data ingestion, using Dataflow to read the predictions from the model

stem: A retailer's demand-forecasting model was accurate at launch, but six months later its predictions are noticeably worse because customer behavior has changed. Which Google Cloud capability addresses this at the model management stage?

choices.text: Pub/Sub, which retries message delivery when a subscriber is slow
Model Monitoring on Agent Platform, which watches input and prediction data for drift and skew and tells the team when to retrain
Cloud NGFW, which blocks unwanted network traffic
Cloud Storage Nearline, a storage class that lowers the cost of keeping data that is read about once a month

stem: A company's data science team trains many versions of a churn model and is losing track of which version is in production, how each performed and how to roll back. Which Google Cloud capability should be used in the model management stage?

choices.text: Cloud Run, a service that runs a stateless container in response to incoming web requests
Dataflow, a service that transforms data records in streaming and batch pipelines at scale for analytics teams
Pub/Sub, a service that holds a queue of messages until a subscriber reads them
Model Registry on Agent Platform, a central repository that tracks, evaluates and deploys model versions

stem: A team repeats the same steps every month: prepare new data, retrain the model, evaluate it and deploy it if it passes. The leader wants this to run automatically and reproducibly instead of by hand. Which Google Cloud capability is meant for this?

choices.text: Pipelines on Agent Platform, which orchestrates ML workflow steps as an automated, repeatable pipeline
Looker dashboards, which display a chart of how often the model was retrained and how it scored
A shared spreadsheet where analysts tick off each step by hand as they finish it each month
Cloud DNS, which maps domain names to IP addresses

stem: A company maps its Google Cloud tools to ML lifecycle stages. Which TWO mappings are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Model training: Pub/Sub
Data ingestion: Model Registry, a store for versions
Model deployment: Looker Studio dashboards that chart results
Model management: Model Monitoring and Model Registry on Agent Platform
Data preparation: Dataflow or BigQuery

stem: A new team's first generative AI pilot produced poor results. A review found that the team skipped data preparation and fed raw, inconsistent records directly into training. What is the most accurate lesson?

choices.text: Preparation is optional, because larger models automatically detect and correct inconsistent or duplicate records
Preparation matters only after deployment, once the model is being monitored in production
The quality of what the model learns depends on the quality of the data, so cleaning, standardizing and organizing data comes before training
The only fix is to switch from supervised to reinforcement learning

stem: A manager hears that Gemini is "multimodal" and asks the team what advantages that brings compared with a text-only model for a customer-support tool. Which TWO benefits are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The model no longer needs any prompt, because images replace instructions
Customers can send a screenshot of an error together with a question, and the model can interpret both
The model works only with image inputs, so text tickets must be converted into pictures first
The model is guaranteed never to make mistakes about content shown in images
One model can handle several kinds of input such as text and images, instead of requiring a separate model for each input type

stem: A CFO asks the team to explain "training" versus "inference" in simple terms so that cost discussions make sense. Which explanation is accurate?

choices.text: Training is when a model answers user questions, and inference is when it is first loaded with a dataset
Training is when a model learns patterns from data; inference is when the trained model produces output for new inputs
Training and inference are two names for the same step of sending a prompt to a model
Training is when employees learn to use the tool, and inference is when the vendor invoices the company

stem: A consumer-goods company wants its marketing team to type a short description of a campaign idea and receive original product-style pictures to review the same day. Which kind of foundation model matches the modality of this need?

choices.text: A text-only large language model, because the campaign idea is written as text and the answer can be a written layout description
A speech recognition model, because it turns what the team says about the campaign idea into written words
An image generation model, because the input is a text description and the required output is a new picture
A classification model trained on past campaign results, because it scores which ideas are likely to perform well

stem: An insurer wants one AI assistant that reads a claimant's typed description, photos of vehicle damage and a scanned repair estimate, and then drafts a summary for the adjuster. Which model characteristic is most important for this use case?

choices.text: Support for generating video, so that the assistant can replay the accident from the photos
A very small model size, so that the assistant can run on an adjuster's phone without network access
Audio transcription only, since the claimant's description is the most important input
Multimodal capability, so a single model can interpret text and images together in one request

stem: A law firm wants a model to summarize contracts that run to hundreds of pages and to answer questions that depend on clauses in different sections of the same contract. Which model selection factor matters most for keeping the whole contract in view?

choices.text: The context window, since it limits how much text the model can consider in one request
The temperature setting, since higher values make the summary of each section more detailed
The number of languages in the interface, since contract text is read in the console
The model's image generation quality, since contracts include signature blocks and stamps

stem: A healthcare provider is selecting a model platform for summarizing clinician notes. Its compliance team requires that customer prompts and notes are not used to train the provider's models without permission, and that the provider keeps control of where its data is processed. Which TWO considerations should guide the choice? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Whether the vendor allows prompts to be shared with other customers to improve answer quality
Whether the platform offers data governance controls, such as choosing the processing location and customer-managed encryption keys
Whether the model has the highest score on a public leaderboard, since that guarantees compliance with healthcare rules
Whether the model name is widely recognized, because brand familiarity lowers regulatory risk
Whether the platform commits not to use customer data to train or fine-tune models without the customer's permission

stem: A bank is planning a customer-facing assistant that must answer questions every hour of every day and handle sharp rises in traffic when a promotion launches. The bank has no team to run model servers. Which selection factor does this requirement describe, and what approach fits?

choices.text: Modality, met by choosing a model that supports audio so that customers can call in
Context window, met by choosing the model that accepts the longest prompt
Availability and reliability, met by using a managed model service that Google operates and scales
Fine-tuning depth, met by retraining the model weights on the bank's own servers before every promotion

stem: A telecom company wants to tag millions of short customer messages each day as billing, outage or cancellation. The labels are simple, answers are needed within a fraction of a second, and cost per request must stay low. Which model choice best balances performance and cost?

choices.text: No model at all, because gen AI can never be used for classification
A video generation model, because it can process high volumes of requests in parallel
The largest and most capable model available, since higher capability always gives the best business result
A smaller, faster and lower-cost model, tested on a sample of real messages to confirm that accuracy is good enough

stem: A retailer's team finds that a general foundation model writes product descriptions that are accurate but do not use the brand's tone or its internal terminology. They have a few thousand approved descriptions written by brand editors. Which TWO steps are reasonable approaches to customization? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Start by improving the prompt with instructions and examples of the brand voice, and measure the result
Train a new foundation model from scratch on the few thousand descriptions, since that is the cheapest route
Delete the approved descriptions so that the model is not biased by the brand's own writing
Switch to an image generation model, because brand tone is a visual property
Consider tuning the model on the approved descriptions if prompt changes do not give consistent results

stem: A software company wants its developers to describe a function in plain language and receive draft code, plus explanations of unfamiliar code. Which category of gen AI use case is this?

choices.text: Summarizing, because the model reduces long code files to a short abstract
Automating a payroll process, because the model replaces the developers' entire workflow
Discovering, because the model searches the internet for existing programs
Creating, because the model generates new code from a natural-language description

stem: A contact-center director wants supervisors to review 20,000 recorded calls a week without listening to each one. The supervisors need a short account of each call: the customer's issue, what was done and how it ended. Which gen AI use case category fits best?

choices.text: Automating, because the model replaces supervisors in coaching decisions without human involvement
Creating, because the model produces new marketing images from each call
Summarizing, because the model condenses long call content into short, structured accounts
Discovering, because the model finds the physical location of the customer

stem: Employees at a manufacturer waste hours looking for answers in thousands of internal manuals, policies and slide decks stored in many places. The company wants them to ask questions in plain language and get answers with links to the source documents. Which gen AI use case category is this?

choices.text: Discovering, because it helps people find information across a large body of content
Automating, because the solution removes the need for the manufacturer's documentation department and its editors
Summarizing only, because a gen AI solution can condense documents but cannot return links to them
Creating, because the solution produces new manuals for each employee on request

stem: An online retailer receives thousands of routine emails each day such as "where is my order" and "how do I return this item". It wants a gen AI agent to draft and send answers using order data, and to hand unusual or sensitive cases to a person. Which use case category does this describe?

choices.text: Discovering, because the agent looks for new customers in competitor data
Automating, because the agent takes over repeatable service tasks while people handle exceptions
Creating, because the agent produces a brand-new product line
Summarizing, because the agent condenses each email into a one-line note for staff and never replies

stem: A regional sales director wants managers without data-science skills to ask questions such as "which product lines fell short of plan last quarter and why?" in plain language and get a clear written answer from the company's sales figures. Which gen AI capability describes this use case?

choices.text: Speech synthesis, which reads the sales table aloud to the managers without analysing the figures
Image generation, which draws a new logo for each product line
Video generation, which turns each sales figure into a short film for the managers
Natural-language data analysis, which lets non-specialists query and interpret data

stem: A media company plans to use gen AI on its content. Which TWO of its holdings are unstructured data? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A spreadsheet of ad revenue with a fixed set of numeric columns per month
A relational table of subscribers with columns for ID, plan type and renewal date
Thousands of recorded interviews and podcast episodes stored as audio files
A database of invoices with fixed fields for amount, date and customer number
Millions of archived news photographs and scanned print articles

stem: A bank has two data stores: a transaction table in a warehouse with fixed fields, and a large archive of customer emails and call transcripts. A leader asks what the difference means for planning gen AI work. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The transaction table cannot be used by any AI system, because it is organized, while the archive is ready without review
The table is easy to query, while the emails and transcripts hold rich content models can read but that needs governance and quality checks
The emails and transcripts are structured data, because they contain complete sentences
Both stores need identical handling, because gen AI treats structured and unstructured data in exactly the same way

stem: A team is preparing a data set of support emails so that a model can learn to sort new emails into categories. Each email in the set carries a tag written by an agent, such as "refund" or "technical fault". How is this data best described?

choices.text: Labeled data, because each email is paired with the correct answer the model should learn
Synthetic data, because agents have artificially generated new emails to add to the real ones
Streaming data, because emails arrive continuously through the whole day
Unlabeled data, because emails are free text without a table

stem: A manufacturer wants a model to write plain-language summaries of maintenance reports. It has years of reports but no one has ever written reference summaries, and it has no budget for a large labeling project. Which approach fits this data situation?

choices.text: Pause the project until staff manually label every report with a model-ready category and summary
Collect labels by asking the model to label its own mistakes, with no human check
Start from a pre-trained foundation model and guide it with prompts and a few examples
Build a supervised model from scratch on the reports, since supervised learning does not need labels

stem: A retailer's customer table has many records with a missing email address, missing postal code or missing birth date. A team wants to use it for personalized recommendations. Which data quality characteristic is the problem, and what is the business effect?

choices.text: Cost, because a table with missing fields is always cheaper to store and so is the better choice
Format, because the table is stored in a database instead of a text file
Availability, because the table can only be read by the team between midnight and six each day
Completeness, because gaps in required fields limit how well the model can personalize

stem: A global distributor merged three regional systems. The same product appears as "12 oz", "12oz." and "twelve ounces", and dates appear as day-month-year in one system and month-day-year in another. The team's AI assistant gives conflicting answers about stock. Which data quality characteristic was violated, and what should the team do?

choices.text: Consistency; agree on standard units and formats, then clean the merged data
Completeness; add random values to every empty column
Relevance; delete the older regional systems and retrain the assistant on newly collected data
Availability; ask the vendor to restart the assistant every hour

stem: A human-resources team builds a gen AI assistant to answer employee questions about current leave and benefits policy. It loads a collection of old marketing brochures, last decade's policy drafts and press releases because that was the easiest data to export. Answers are often off-topic or outdated. Which data characteristic is mainly at fault?

choices.text: Format, because brochures use fonts that models cannot read
Relevance, because the data does not match the task and is outdated
Completeness, because every file lacks a title page
Cost, because exporting files from storage always has a price that the HR team must pay

stem: A financial firm has customer feedback in a call-center system, contracts in a document archive, and sales figures in another department's database. Each team guards its data, and analysts wait weeks for access. The firm wants to use gen AI across all three. Which TWO actions best improve data accessibility while respecting governance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Catalog the data sources and bring them into a governed, discoverable platform
Copy the three data sets to each analyst's laptop so no one waits for permissions
Remove all access restrictions on the data to speed up the project
Delete the oldest records in every system so that there is less data to share
Define access controls and policies that give authorized users and systems the right level of access

stem: An insurer wants to use ten years of claims paperwork for gen AI. Much of it is scanned paper forms, handwritten notes and files in several incompatible formats. A project sponsor asks what this means for planning. Which answer is most accurate?

choices.text: The project should ignore the handwritten notes and the oldest forms, because they always lower the overall quality of results
Format matters: converting the files costs time and money, so budget for preparation and test a sample
Format has no effect, because a foundation model automatically reads every file type with perfect accuracy
The project should be cancelled, because scanned paper can never be used for gen AI

stem: A company tunes a model to route customer complaints. It paid two outsourcing teams to label 5,000 complaints, but one team tags delivery delays as "logistics" and the other tags the same issue as "shipping". After tuning, the model routes similar complaints unpredictably. What is the most likely cause, and what is the best response?

choices.text: The model has too few parameters, so the company should discard the labeled data and begin again with a new model
The complaints are unstructured, so tuning can never work on them and the project should end
The labeled data is inconsistent, so the company should write shared labeling guidelines and relabel or reconcile the conflicting examples
The complaints are too recent, so the company should wait a year and then retrain on the same labels

stem: A compliance officer asks what "grounding" means when the company's engineers say they will ground the new assistant. Which explanation is most accurate?

choices.text: Retraining the model from scratch on all company documents so that the facts are stored permanently in its weights
Running the assistant on isolated infrastructure so that user prompts never leave the company's own private network
Limiting the assistant to a short list of pre-written answers so that it cannot generate any new sentences for a user
Connecting the model's output to verifiable sources of information so answers are anchored to that data instead of invented

stem: A bank plans three assistants. The first answers staff questions about internal lending policies. The second explains a licensed market-data provider's research reports that the bank pays for. The third answers general questions about this week's public regulatory announcements. Which pairing of grounding data source to assistant is correct?

choices.text: Internal policies are enterprise data, licensed research is third-party data, and public announcements are world data
Internal policies are world data, licensed research is enterprise data, and public announcements are third-party data
Internal policies are enterprise data, licensed research is world data, and public announcements are third-party data
Internal policies are third-party data, licensed research is world data, and public announcements are enterprise data

stem: A product owner wants to explain to executives how retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) changes what happens when an employee asks the assistant a question. Which description is most accurate?

choices.text: The question is sent to several models at once and the reply that most of them agree on is shown to the employee
Relevant passages are retrieved from a data source and added to the prompt, so the model writes its answer using that material
The model replies as usual, and a separate filter then deletes any sentence it cannot match to a stored document
The model is retrained overnight on the new question and answer, then replies from its updated weights the next day

stem: A manufacturer's support assistant gives fluent answers, but auditors say nobody can verify where a statement came from. Which change to the way the assistant is built best addresses the auditors' concern?

choices.text: Switch on stricter safety settings so that the model blocks any answer that discusses product faults or warranty claims
Increase the maximum output length so that every answer includes a longer explanation of the reasoning behind each statement
Raise the temperature so that the assistant produces several differently worded answers and the user picks the best one
Ground the assistant in the manufacturer's manuals with RAG so that each answer is based on retrieved passages and can link back to them

stem: A travel company wants its chat assistant to answer questions about this week's flight disruptions and newly announced visa rules. This information is public and changes daily, and the company does not keep it in its own systems. Which grounding approach fits best?

choices.text: Fine-tuning the model on last year's customer chat logs so that it learns typical travel questions and the usual answers to them
A RAG corpus built from the visa rules that the legal team copied into a spreadsheet the last time they reviewed the topic
Grounding with Google Search, so the model uses current results from Google's search engine for its answer and shows the sources
Pre-built RAG over a data store of the company's own brochures, indexed once and refreshed only when marketing publishes a new catalog

stem: A retailer licenses product reviews from a data vendor, which exposes them through the vendor's own search service. The retailer wants its assistant to answer from that licensed content without copying the whole dataset into Google Cloud. Which approach matches the need?

choices.text: Ground the model through the vendor's search service, by connecting it with a grounding option that accepts an external search API
Use Grounding with Agent Search and upload every vendor review into a data store so the vendor service is never queried
Ground the model with Grounding with Google Search, because public web results are the closest substitute for the vendor's data
Fine-tune the model on a sample of the licensed reviews, then retire the vendor's search service once the model has been trained

stem: A public-sector agency has two needs. Team one wants an intranet question-answering assistant live quickly, with Google handling indexing and answer generation over its websites and documents. Team two is building its own application and wants configurable control over how its documents are chunked, embedded and retrieved before the prompt is built. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Team one uses a configurable RAG Engine, and team two uses the pre-built RAG experience of Agent Search
Both teams use fine-tuning, because only fine-tuning lets a model answer from the agency's own documents
Both teams use Grounding with Google Search, since search results can be adjusted for each application
Team one uses the pre-built RAG of Agent Search, and team two uses RAG APIs for a custom pipeline

stem: A leadership team reviews the expected benefits of grounding the company's assistant in its own knowledge base. Select TWO benefits that grounding is designed to provide. (Select TWO)

choices.text: It makes the model's weights permanently contain every document that is added to the knowledge base
It lowers the chance of invented answers by anchoring responses to the supplied data sources
It removes the need for any human review of answers about regulated or high-risk topics
It guarantees that the knowledge base itself is always complete, current and free of errors
It lets responses include links to the sources used, so reviewers can check a statement

stem: A company grounded its HR assistant in the policy library. An employee receives a confident answer that quotes a leave rule the company replaced last year. Searching the library shows the old policy document is still indexed next to the new one. Select TWO actions that most directly address the cause. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Raise the temperature so the model explores more answer variations and is more likely to land on the newer rule
Set the safety settings to their strictest level so the assistant refuses questions about leave
Remove or retire the outdated document from the knowledge base so that retrieval cannot return it
Fine-tune the model again on the old policy so that it learns that the rule has changed and ignores it
Add a review process so that policy owners keep the indexed documents current as policies change

stem: A bank's assistant explains fee schedules to customers, and every answer must stay consistent and close to the supplied policy text. A pilot shows the wording and even some details change noticeably between repeated asks of the same question. Which adjustment to the generation parameters is most appropriate?

choices.text: Turn off the safety settings so that the model is not distracted from the fee schedule by content filtering
Raise the temperature so that the model considers many less likely words and then settles on the most common one
Lower the temperature so that the model picks the most probable words more often and its answers vary less
Raise the maximum output length so that the model repeats each fee detail several times in different words

stem: A marketing team uses a model to brainstorm slogans and campaign names. The team complains that every run returns nearly identical, predictable ideas. Which change to the sampling settings is most likely to help?

choices.text: Raise the temperature so that less likely words are chosen more often and the ideas become more varied
Shorten the maximum output length so that the model has less room to repeat the same ideas
Lower the temperature to its minimum so that the model always selects the single most probable word
Tighten the safety settings so that the model has to avoid its usual phrasing and invent new ones

stem: A product manager is told that the team can adjust "top-p" in addition to temperature. Which statement describes what top-p does?

choices.text: It sets the strictness with which harmful content categories are blocked in both the prompt and the response
It chooses how many retrieved passages from the knowledge base are added to the prompt before the model answers
It sets the largest number of tokens that the model is allowed to write in a single response before it stops
It selects the next word from the smallest group of most probable candidates whose combined probability reaches the top-p value

stem: A legal team uses a model to summarize long contracts. Users report that summaries often stop in the middle of a sentence, even though the prompt is clear and the content is correct up to that point. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The safety settings are too loose, so the fix is to block more categories until the model finishes its sentences
The maximum output length is too small, so the fix is to allow more output tokens or to ask for a shorter summary
The grounding source is incomplete, so the fix is to add more contracts to the knowledge base the model searches
The temperature is set too low, so the fix is to raise it until the model chooses to continue past the stopping point

stem: A children's education company builds a homework helper on a Gemini model. Leadership wants the tool to block harmful content such as harassment or dangerous instructions in what the tool replies. Which setting addresses this?

choices.text: Lower the temperature to its minimum, since a deterministic model cannot produce harmful or inappropriate content
Reduce the maximum output tokens, because shorter replies contain fewer words that could be considered harmful
Configure safety settings with blocking thresholds for harmful content categories, which filter unsafe responses before they reach children
Ground the model in the school curriculum only, since grounded models are prevented from generating unsafe content

stem: A pharmaceutical company wants a research assistant that explains dosing documents accurately and a separate assistant that drafts upbeat internal newsletters. Select TWO configurations that suit the two assistants. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Dosing assistant: a very small maximum output length so that every dosing answer is a single short sentence
Newsletter assistant: a moderately higher temperature so that drafts vary and read as lively, with an editor review
Dosing assistant: ungrounded, with a high temperature so the model can phrase each dosing rule creatively
Newsletter assistant: temperature at its minimum and top-p at its minimum so that every draft reads identically
Dosing assistant: grounded in the approved dosing documents, with a low temperature and human review of answers

stem: A product manager asks why the company's new customer-service agent needs "tools" at all, since the underlying language model is already very capable. Which answer is most accurate?

choices.text: Tools replace the language model's reasoning, so the agent follows a fixed script and never has to interpret what the customer is asking
Tools are only needed for security, because they block the model from answering questions that fall outside the company's approved topics
Tools retrain the model every night on the day's conversations, so that the agent remembers each customer's order history in its weights
A model on its own only generates text from what it learned in training, so tools let the agent fetch current information and take real actions in other systems

stem: A bank's developers want the model to decide when to look up an account balance, but the bank's security team insists that the call to the core banking system be made by the bank's own application code, never by the agent platform. Which tool approach fits?

choices.text: Function calling, where the model returns the function name and arguments and the bank's application runs the call and returns the result
Prompt tuning, which teaches the model the balances of every account so that no external call is needed
An OpenAPI tool configured with the banking system's schema, so the agent calls the system directly on the customer's behalf
A data store of exported balances, which the agent searches by meaning and quotes in its answers

stem: An insurer wants an agent to answer policyholder questions from 4,000 PDF policy documents and claims guides, which are updated each quarter. The agent must retrieve the relevant passages, and no business transaction has to be performed. Which kind of tool fits best?

choices.text: A code-execution tool that lets the agent write and run programs to calculate the premium for every question
A function tool that the policyholder's browser runs to write each new PDF's text into the model's prompt
An API tool connected to the claims system, so that the agent can create and update claims for the policyholder
A data store tool that indexes the documents so the agent can retrieve passages and ground its answers in them

stem: A logistics company is designing a shipping assistant. Select TWO of the planned capabilities that need an action tool (an API or function call) rather than a data store alone. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Booking a pickup slot in the company's scheduling system when the customer confirms
Explaining the differences between delivery service levels as described in the help centre
Summarising the terms of the company's standard shipping contract on request
Answering questions about the packaging rules published in the company's handbook
